message: Tool input chooses the URL fetched by confluence_fetcher.confluence._session.get. Without an allowlist the agent can be made to call internal services (for example http://169.254.169.254 or localhost admin APIs).
fix: Optional hardening: validate attachment_id against ^(att)?\d+$ before building the URL.
reason: Not SSRF: the host comes from the operator's Confluence URL (config.url); attachment_id only lands in the path of a GET on that same Confluence server, which the caller can already query with the same credentials.

message: Tool input chooses the URL fetched by confluence_fetcher.confluence._session.get. Without an allowlist the agent can be made to call internal services (for example http://169.254.169.254 or localhost admin APIs).
fix: Hardening: reject download URLs whose host differs from config.url before sending the authenticated session there.
reason: download_url is not a tool argument: it is the _links.download value returned by the configured Confluence server's own attachment metadata (normally a relative path joined to config.url). A tool caller cannot pick the host.

message: Tool input chooses the URL fetched by confluence_fetcher.confluence._session.get. Without an allowlist the agent can be made to call internal services (for example http://169.254.169.254 or localhost admin APIs).
fix: Hardening: same-host check against config.url before fetching with the authenticated session.
reason: The URL comes from the attachment list returned by the configured Confluence server (get_content_attachments), not from the content_id argument; the caller cannot choose the host.

title: confluence_upload_attachment(s) reads any file on the server host and uploads it to Confluence
reason: file_path (and each entry of file_paths) is a tool argument opened with no base-directory check, unlike the download paths which use validate_safe_path; an injected instruction can upload ~/.ssh/id_rsa, .env or /proc/self/environ (holding the Atlassian tokens) to a page the attacker can read.
fix: Run every path through validate_safe_path(path, UPLOAD_BASE_DIR) with a dedicated operator-configured upload directory (realpath + is_relative_to), and reject absolute paths outside it.

title: jira_update_issue attachments argument reads any file on the server host and attaches it to an issue
reason: Paths from the attachments argument go to upload_attachment, which only makes them absolute and checks existence before opening; a prompt-injected update_issue call can attach any readable server file (keys, env, token cache) to an attacker-visible issue.
fix: Validate each path with validate_safe_path against a configured upload directory before opening; refuse anything outside it.

title: HTTP transports bind 0.0.0.0 and unauthenticated requests fall back to the operator's global Atlassian credentials

evidence.quote: # Fallback to global fetcher if not in HTTP context or no user info

reason: With --transport sse/streamable-http, a request with no Authorization header is not rejected and tools run with the server's own configured token (confused deputy), on all interfaces by default; anyone who can reach the port gets the operator's Jira/Confluence access plus the file-reading upload tools above.
fix: Require an Authorization header (or a server-side shared secret) on HTTP transports when no per-user auth is given, default HOST to 127.0.0.1, and check Origin/Host. User must confirm whether HTTP mode is deployed and who can reach it.

title: Jira/Confluence content returned to the model unmarked, with exfil-capable write tools in the same server
reason: Issue and page text written by any project member reaches the model as plain tool output; combined with M001/M002 the same server can read local files and post them back to Atlassian, a full untrusted-input -> private-data -> exfil path with no approval beyond the client's.
fix: Fix M001/M002 first; document READ_ONLY_MODE / ENABLED_TOOLS for untrusted content, and keep write tools behind client approval.
